Marathon Petroleum rose 2.48% today after a sharp four-day climb that added $35 to the stock price. The rally coincides with oil prices stabilizing around $90 a barrel and refineries running at 95.2% capacity—near maximum utilization. With crude supplies ample (the IEA reports global markets back in surplus after Russian production rebounded) and fuel inventories steady, the refining sector benefits from the combination of steady input costs and sustained demand, which supports margins for refiners like Marathon.

The broader context is a shift in oil market sentiment: Trump administration comments about Iran de-escalation had briefly spooked the market in early November, pushing Brent below $90, but prices have since recovered as the geopolitical uncertainty eased without collapsing demand. Refineries are operating near flat-out, and gasoline and diesel stocks remain at levels that suggest healthy product demand, which is what keeps refiner profitability intact.
